translations.text: For we [?] are from God. For destruction has overcome your soul, even to the point of death.
It is not good to scheme against purity before God. For the great demonic frenzy of the torture you inflict has cast you into blasphemy.
For the angel whom the Lord and God Jesus Christ sent
shut the mouths of [?]—the angel whom you, in your arrogance, turned into Apollo.
Aurelian became angry and ordered them to be struck on the jaws with lead balls,
saying to him, “Do not answer foolishly and arrogantly. Know that you are standing before the emperor.”
After having Paul taken outside the tribunal, he summoned Juliana and said to her,
“Juliana, mistress of my soul, let me persuade you.
Do not be deceived by the folly of your brother Paul. For I see that you are a wise maiden
and possess great wisdom. So take comfort and listen to me,
and you will be mistress of my soul. I will erect golden images of you in every city throughout the whole world.”
Juliana answered, “I will not turn away, Aurelian, you torturer and ungodly man.
You will not deceive the servant of God Most High. Do not devise eternal death for me, seeking to deprive me
of Christ’s glory and the kingdom of heaven, to which you are a stranger.” He had her taken away and ordered Paul to be brought in.
He said to him, “Paul, your sister Juliana has promised to sacrifice to the gods
and to become my wife and mistress of my empire.
So be willing to think the same way yourself, and come forward and sacrifice to the gods.” Paul said, “You have indeed lied.
You have done nothing foreign to the teaching of your father the devil. For you cannot draw anyone away
except through lies. But you will not snatch us away, even if you promise us a kingdom
of which you yourself are deprived.” Aurelian said, “How long will you insult me without shame, you fool and madman?
By the gods, I will torture you both so that no one will be able to help you.” He ordered fire to be brought,
along with iron rods, and ordered them to be put into the fire, and Paul’s hands and feet to be bound,
and an iron stake to be thrust between his hands and feet and driven into the ground,
and him to be beaten with two [?] clubs [?]. He ordered Juliana to be placed in a brothel, that is, a place of prostitution.
Many of the crowd standing there came running, competing with one another.
who would go in to her first. For they were like horses neighing over the beauty
of her. When she had taken her place where Aurelian had commanded,
an angel of the Lord immediately appeared before her, saying, “Do not be afraid, Juliana.
For the Lord Jesus Christ, whom you serve, has sent me to protect you and to reveal his holy name to all who fear him.”
And as all the crowds rushed toward Juliana out of desire for her,
the angel shook off dust as though from their feet and blinded them, and they did not know where they were going.
They could not approach her, and all the crowds cried out together, saying,
“Great is the God of Paul and Juliana, who everywhere is the savior and protector of those who fear him.”
They remained blind, and they came and bowed down before her,
crying out and saying, “Juliana, servant of God Most High,
we have sinned foolishly against you. But forgive us, as a servant of the good God.
Pray to Christ that he may grant us sight.” Saint Juliana, moved with compassion, took a little water
and raised her eyes to heaven and prayed to God, saying, “Lord Jesus Christ, Savior of all people,
hear me and show the wonders you perform for human beings, and grant them sight,
so that they may glorify your holy and most praiseworthy name.” And so she sprinkled all the people,
and all those who had been blinded regained their sight. They ran into the church of Christ and repented, glorifying God
and confessing their sins, and became Christians. Meanwhile, Saint Paul was severely tortured
and beaten with iron rods, for they had been heated and were shining like lightning.
He cried out, saying, “Aurelian, you torturer and impious man,
what evil have I done that you torture me so cruelly and impiously? For Christ gives me relief from the tortures,
but he will make you share in the eternal fire prepared for you and the devil.”
Aurelian said, “Where is your sister, whom you claim to be a virgin?
Look, I have sent her to prostitution, so that all who wish may have intercourse with her. Is she still a virgin?”
Saint Paul said, “I trust in God, who eases my suffering
and delivers me from all your evil schemes, that he will protect her too.”
For he sent his angel from the heights of heaven to protect her. And behold, she returns to see my chains, keeping her virginity pure and undefiled.
And Aurelian ordered Saint Juliana to be brought in. And when she came to the judgment seat,
Paul saw her, was filled with joy, and smiled. But Aurelian said:
"Have your lovers had their fill of your beauty?" Juliana said, "My beauty, adornment, and loveliness are Christ,
who sent his angel and sheltered me, poor as I am, because I put my trust in him.
And I praise his holy name, for he is the God who works wonders, and there is no other besides him."
And Aurelian ordered Paul to be untied and a pit nine cubits deep to be dug in the ground,
and wood and fire to be brought and burned in the pit. While he was speaking, they dug the pit and brought wood and fire,
and lit a fire in the pit. Then he ordered Paul and Juliana to be thrown into the fire.
As the two went, they blessed God and prayed to the Savior Jesus Christ, their helper.
And when they reached the place, they marked their faces with the sign of Christ's cross.
And they threw them into the fire. And the two were in the fire, singing and praising God.
And behold, an angel of the Lord came down from heaven and shook out the furnace with its fire.
And he did not allow the fire to harm them. And the two sang, blessing God in the blazing, fiery pit,
saying, "Blessed are you, Lord God of all ages, the immortal one,
who remembered our lowliness, though we are unworthy because of our sins. Being [?]
and good, appear to us both to quench the power of the fire and the fury of the tormentor Aurelian."
And the crowds standing at a distance heard the two of them, for many were praying to God for them.
Thus many of the pagans also repented and opened their hearts because of the two saints,
and turned away from idol worship and believed in Christ.
And many of the executioners who were torturing the two saints at Aurelian's command, seeing the mighty works performed by God,
believed in God. And they reported to Aurelian everything that had happened. And he ordered the two who were there in the pit to be stoned.
And behold, suddenly there was a roar and thunder from heaven, with many flashes of lightning and clouds moving, full of fire.
And the clouds came as far as Aurelian and stopped, and poured fire onto the earth.
And a voice from heaven said, "Aurelian, into the fiery generation!"

and thrown into prison. And the two of them were praising God for the miracles he had performed for them.
After seven days, Aurelian came out and sat on the judgment seat. They brought all the idols he had,
silver and gold, adorned with precious stones. And he arranged
them in order, spreading royal purple cloth beneath their feet.
And he said, “Summon Paul and Juliana, and place them before the judgment seat.”
And threatening them, he said, “Come forward and sacrifice to the gods. Do not hope to escape my hands.”
But Saint Paul smiled and said, “I will not abandon God, who made heaven and earth,
and bow down to idols.” Aurelian said, “You deserve a wretched death, you wicked man!
Do they seem to you to be idols, and not gods? Do you not see what they are like?” Saint Paul answered, “This Zeus,
whom you consider to be a god, was a man, a disciple of Satan, thoroughly trained in the arts of sorcery.
He was a fornicator far beyond all other living people. Seeing men's beautiful wives and daughters,
he desired them, spoke to them [?], and had intercourse with them. He induced them to honor him as a god,
changing his form through his skill in sorcery. Sometimes he transformed himself into a bull,
and sometimes he took the likeness of winged birds, an eagle or a stork. Through these transformations he seduced women of noble birth.
For to some he appeared transformed into gold, promising wealth.
But let me not recount everything in order, for I know that you are becoming angry.
And this one beside Zeus, called Apollo—was he not born of fornication, from a woman named Leto?
Did she not give birth to him in the wilderness of Asia, between two oak trees?
He too committed wicked deeds, imitating his father. Likewise Dionysus,
your renowned god—was he not also born of fornication, being born of Semele, the daughter of Cadmus?”
Aurelian said, “You wicked fool! From Cronus and Rhea are born the mothers of the gods.”
Paul smiled and said, “Then is someone who has a wife a god?”
Aurelian said, “You wicked fool! How long will you speak blasphemies against the gods, uttering so much nonsense
and insulting them? But your Christ, whom you Christians say is the heavenly God—
Was he not born of a woman? Saint Paul answered: “You are not worthy to hear the mysteries of God,
lest you deceive some of those standing here with your falsehoods and destroy them.
It must be said: In the beginning God created heaven and earth and everything on them.
Last of all, he created man in his own image, which consists in goodwill,
innocence, blamelessness, righteousness, and reverence for God. And he placed him in the paradise of delight. After some time had passed,
God said: ‘It is not good for man to be alone. Let us make him a helper like himself.’
‘Let us make’ means the Father and the Son, for the Father does nothing without the Son,
nor does the Son do anything without the Father. And it says: ‘The Lord brought a deep sleep upon Adam,’
and, taking one of his ribs, he made him a wife from his own body.
And Eve was with Adam in paradise. When the devil saw her, he became envious and brought ruin upon them both.
For Adam had gone away to that place in paradise, leaving Eve alone.
The devil approached and, taking the form of a serpent, deceived her. And that woman deceived Adam.
Both of them had become disobedient to God, and they were driven away from the food of paradise
to work the ground with their own hands. Taking on a life of toil, they lived nine hundred
and thirty years, having sons and daughters, from whom the whole world was populated.
When Adam met his end because of his disobedience, after nine hundred and thirty years,
and all our fathers had been brought down to Hades to live in death,
there was no distinction between the righteous and the sinful. The righteous were like the ungodly,
and the sinful were like the righteous. As the blessed apostle Paul, the light of the Church, testified, saying:
‘Death reigned from Adam even to Moses, and not over those who sinned.’
But after many generations, God in heaven heard the groans and prayers of those held captive by Hades
and, through his Word, who is his only-begotten Son,
was pleased, according to his plan, to assume human nature and undo disobedience through obedience.
As John testifies about him, saying: ‘In the beginning was the Word,
and the Word was from God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning from God. All things came into being through him.’
And without him not one thing came into being that has come into being. This, then, is God, the heavenly Word, the Father's Son,
who is the Father's power and wisdom and the right hand of the Most High. He is announced by Gabriel the archangel
to the holy and most pure virgin of royal lineage, named Mary, with these words:
“The Holy Spirit will enter into you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore the holy one born of you
will be called the Son of God.” And he is born of the Holy Spirit
and of the spotless and most pure virgin, for the ordering and salvation of the world. For no one
could see the bodiless God with his own eyes, for God is a consuming fire.
And no human being who has seen God will remain alive. Therefore, for the sake of this ordering,
Christ was born in the flesh, and he grows in age according to the flesh.
And he lives among human beings as a human being for more than thirty years,
going about the towns and villages, showing kindness to all those afflicted by the devil.
And afterward he is nailed to the wood of the cross, suffering for the salvation of the world,
to save the world that had perished through the devil's deception. And he dies in his humanity
and is buried, while remaining forever perfect, existing before all this, neither nailed to the cross nor subject to suffering,
but immortal and eternally existing in his divinity. And on the third day, having risen from the dead, he appeared to his disciples,
that is, the holy apostles, and to many who had truly believed in him, living among them,
eating and drinking with the apostles for forty days. And he ascended into heaven and sat down at the Father's right hand
with the flesh that had been united with God the Word. And therefore Satan, seeing this,
suffers in his defeat, for Christ crushed him beneath human feet. And human beings, by the grace
of God, enter the kingdom of heaven, of which you are deprived.
For you have a share in the lot of the fiery race, and you are a partner of your father, the devil.
Hearing this, Aurelian's face kept changing color with rage,
and he gnashed his teeth at him, like a lion in a thicket, [?] a wild beast but failing to catch it.
And he answered Saint Paul, saying: “I have waited patiently while you raved at length,
you fool and impious man. How long will you revile and blaspheme the gods? Come forward and sacrifice to the gods.”
But if not, I will destroy you both with a terrible death, and no one will be able to rescue you from my hands.
Paul and Juliana cried out together in a loud voice, saying, “We are Christians,
and we place our hope in Christ. We do not worship demons, and we do not serve your gods.
Nor do we fear your tortures. Devise whatever tortures you wish.
For we trust in God that you will be defeated by us, just as the devil was defeated,
with Christ giving us strength and defeating your cunning schemes.” And Aurelian ordered a large wooden beam to be brought.
It was brought, and he said, “Bind Paul to it.” The servants approached and bound
his hands. And he ordered burning torches to be brought and Paul's face to be scorched,
while the herald cried out, saying, “Do not insult the rulers of the whole world
or blaspheme against the gods.” When Juliana saw her brother being scorched with fire,
she cried out, saying, “Aurelian, you torturer and impious man, why do you torture my brother so cruelly?”
And he ordered her also to be bound to the beam, and burning torches to be brought to her face,
and then to burn her all over her body. Aurelian said, “Shameless woman,
since you are a woman, show modesty, as women should.” But Juliana smiled and said:
“Truly, Aurelian, I regard you as a good father when you teach me,
saying, ‘Since you are a woman, show modesty.’ For I do stand in awe of my Christ, the Son of the living God,
who is before my face, and I cannot abandon him and worship demons.
Rather, I revere him deeply.” But Aurelian grew furious when he heard all this from her.
And he ordered the servants to apply fire all over the bodies of both of them. While the servants burned them without ceasing,
all the citizens who stood there watching them
cried out, saying, “Sovereign Emperor Aurelian, you judge unjustly! Unjustly
you torture them! They refuse to sacrifice; pronounce sentence on them!”
But Aurelian became afraid of the people, lest they stir up a revolt,
and pronounced sentence on them, ordering their heads to be cut off
and their bodies to be thrown to the dogs, the wild beasts, and the birds of the sky.
Having received this answer on the fourth day of the month of March,
the two went out rejoicing and singing, saying, “He has saved us from those who torment us
and has put those who hate us to shame.” When they had gone outside the city,
Saint Paul begged the executioner to behead Juliana before him.
Saint Juliana made the sign of the cross over her face and joyfully stretched out her neck.
The executioner cut off her head. When Saint Paul saw that his sister had died in the Lord,
he lifted his eyes to heaven and blessed God. Then he made the sign of the cross, stretched out his neck, and was beheaded.
Thus he completed his martyrdom. The bodies of the two saints lay outside the city,
and the Christians were not allowed to take them away, for soldiers had been stationed there to keep watch.
Wild beasts, dogs, and birds of the sky came
and sat around their bodies, so as to keep even the flies
away from them. They did this for seven days and nights, and those beasts neither ate nor drank.
The soldiers who had been stationed there reported everything that had happened to Aurelian.
When he heard it, he said, “Oh, the impious madness of the Christian race!
I could not defeat them even when they were dead!” He sent orders and withdrew the soldiers keeping watch during the night.
When daylight came, the Christians went out, took the bodies of the two saints, and buried them peacefully and with joy,
in the reign of our Lord Jesus Christ, with whom glory be to the Father,
together with the Holy Spirit, now and always and forever and ever. Amen.
